formation.title: The Two Sicilies United
formation.text:
At last, the ancient kingdoms of Naples and Sicily stand united under one crown. For centuries, the Mezzogiorno has been fought over by Normans, Hohenstaufen, Angevins, and Aragonese: each leaving their mark upon the land and its people. Now we must decide what this kingdom shall become.

The southern lands possess the richest farmland in Italy, the busiest ports in the Mediterranean, and a population shaped by every civilization that has touched these shores. But they also suffer from powerful barons who defy royal authority, from corsair raids that menace our coasts, and from the ancient rivalry between island and mainland.

Shall we forge a centralized kingdom under firm royal authority, breaking the power of the barons and building a modern state? Or shall we embrace our heritage as the crossroads of the Mediterranean, where Greek, Arab, Norman, and Latin traditions mingle to create something greater than any single culture could achieve?

This choice unlocks a destiny path in the Traditions tab.

options.text: One crown, one law, one kingdom.

modifiers.name: Crown of the Mezzogiorno
modifiers.text: The Kingdom of the Two Sicilies stands united under a single strong crown. From Naples to Palermo, the royal authority extends unbroken, suppressing baronial factionalism and imposing a centralized administration that brings order to the fractious south. The Mezzogiorno shall know one law, one king, one destiny.

options.text: We are the meeting place of civilizations.

modifiers.name: Crossroads of the Mediterranean
modifiers.text: Heir to Norman, Greek, Arab, and Latin traditions, the Kingdom of the Two Sicilies embraces its identity as the great meeting place of civilizations. Where others see division, we see opportunity: in every foreign merchant who docks at Naples, every craftsman who plies his trade in Palermo, every scholar who studies in our academies.

advances.name: Norman Feudal Cavalry
advances.text: The Norman conquerors of southern Italy brought with them the feudal military traditions of northern France: armored knights who formed the most formidable cavalry in the Mediterranean world.

advances.name: Masseria System
advances.text: The great fortified farmsteads of the Mezzogiorno, the masserie, are the backbone of southern Italy's agricultural wealth: vast estates producing grain, olives, and livestock that feed the Mediterranean.

advances.name: Scuola Medica Salernitana
advances.text: The School of Salerno is the oldest medical school in the Western world, where Greek, Latin, Arab, and Jewish physicians share their knowledge. Its graduates practice medicine across Europe.

advances.name: Coastal Torre Network
advances.text: A chain of watchtowers along the coasts of Sicily and southern Italy provides early warning against Barbary corsair raids and serves as a coordinated defense network.

advances.name: Sicilian Vespers Legacy
advances.text: The memory of the 1282 uprising against Angevin tyranny instills fierce resistance to foreign domination among the people of the Two Sicilies.

event.title: The Legacy of the Vespers
event.text:
On Easter Monday, 1282, the bells of the Church of the Holy Spirit outside Palermo rang for vespers. And the island erupted in revolt. Within six weeks, every Frenchman in Sicily was dead or fled. The Sicilian Vespers was more than a massacre: it was a declaration that the people of this land would not be ruled by foreigners who despised them.

The revolt's aftermath reshaped the Mediterranean. Charles of Anjou lost his island kingdom. Peter of Aragon gained a crown. And Sicily itself learned a hard lesson about the price of independence: that freedom won by blood must be defended by either strength or cunning.

As we study this legacy, what lesson shall we draw from it?

options.text: Freedom is won by those who fight for it.

modifiers.name: Spirit of the Vespers
modifiers.text: The memory of the Sicilian Vespers burns bright: a people who rose against foreign oppression and won their freedom through sheer determination.

modifiers.name: Vespers Diplomacy
modifiers.text: The Sicilian Vespers demonstrated that clever diplomacy and foreign alliances can achieve what rebellion alone cannot: the island secured its freedom by inviting the Crown of Aragon to its defense.

advances.name: Mediterranean Granary
advances.text: Southern Italy and Sicily have been the granary of the Mediterranean since Roman times, exporting vast quantities of wheat, olives, and other foodstuffs across the sea. Grain loaded under royal seal at the caricatori of the coast fetches its price in every port that buys it.

advances.name: Tercio di Napoli
advances.text: Under Spanish influence, the kingdoms of Naples and Sicily adopted the tercio system: disciplined infantry formations combining pike and shot that dominated European battlefields.

advances.name: Studium of Naples
advances.text: Founded by Emperor Frederick II in 1224, the University of Naples is the oldest state-sponsored university in the world: a deliberate challenge to the papal universities of the north.

advances.name: Mezzogiorno Commerce
advances.text: The ports of Naples, Palermo, and Messina handle a vast volume of Mediterranean trade, connecting the agricultural wealth of the south with markets across the known world.

advances.name: Galeazza Reale
advances.text: The Two Sicilies maintains a powerful fleet of war galleys specially designed for Mediterranean combat: heavier and better armed than standard galleys, capable of dominating the contested waters between Italy and North Africa.

advances.name: Baronial Suppression
advances.text: The fractious Mezzogiorno barons who have undermined royal authority for centuries are finally brought to heel through systematic legal and political measures.

advances.name: Dogana delle Pecore
advances.text: The royal sheep customs of Foggia, founded by Alfonso the Magnanimous in 1447, reserves the winter pastures of the Tavoliere for the flocks that come down the drove roads from the Abruzzi every autumn. Under the viceroys millions of sheep make the journey each year, and the fee on every head is among the largest revenues of the crown.

advances.name: San Leucio Silk Works
advances.text: The Royal Colony of San Leucio near Caserta represents a revolutionary experiment in industrial production: a silk manufactory where workers enjoy progressive labor conditions, mandatory education, and communal welfare.

advances.name: Real Marina
advances.text: The Royal Navy of the Two Sicilies, the Real Marina, is expanded and modernized under the Bourbons, fielding frigates and ships of the line to protect the kingdom's extensive coastline.

advances.name: Bourbon Legal Reforms
advances.text: The Bourbon monarchs replace the patchwork of Norman, Angevin, and Spanish legal codes with a unified modern legal system inspired by Enlightenment principles.

event.title: The Bourbon Reforms
event.text:
The Bourbon monarchs have embarked on an ambitious program of reform that would transform the kingdom. Ferdinand has established the Royal Colony of San Leucio, where silk workers enjoy benefits unheard of elsewhere in Europe: mandatory education for boys and girls alike, shorter working hours, running water in every home, and communal provision for the sick and elderly.

But the reforms extend far beyond a single colony. New legal codes drawn from Enlightenment principles aim to replace the patchwork of feudal, Norman, and Spanish law. Royal manufactories spring up to challenge the dominance of northern Italian and French industry. The question is whether to pursue the intellectual promise of these reforms (modernizing education, law, and governance) or to focus on their industrial potential, building the manufactories and infrastructure that could make the Mezzogiorno an economic power.

options.text: Enlighten the minds of our people.

modifiers.name: Bourbon Enlightenment
modifiers.text: The progressive reforms of the Bourbon monarchs have brought modern administration, public education, and rational governance to the kingdom.

options.text: Build the workshops of the future.

modifiers.name: Bourbon Industrial Program
modifiers.text: The crown's program of royal manufactories and infrastructure development transforms the kingdom's economic capacity.

advances.name: Mezzogiorno Industry
advances.text: The industrial development of southern Italy, driven by royal manufactories and infrastructure investment, begins to challenge the traditional dominance of northern Italian economies.

advances.name: Carbonari Legacy
advances.text: The secret societies of the Carbonari, charcoal burners, spread revolutionary ideals of constitutional government and national identity throughout the kingdom, shaping the political consciousness of a generation.

advances.name: Army of the Holy Faith
advances.text: In February 1799 Cardinal Fabrizio Ruffo landed in Calabria with eight companions and no money. By June the peasant masses that gathered under his banner of the cross had marched the length of the kingdom and taken Naples back from the Parthenopean Republic.

destiny.name: Destiny of the Two Sicilies
destiny.text: The Kingdom of the Two Sicilies has been forged. Now its rulers must prove worthy of the crown by bringing stability to this fractious but fertile realm.

event.title: The Destiny of Two Kingdoms
event.text:
The Two Sicilies stand united and stable. The ancient kingdoms of Naples and Sicily, once divided by the narrow Strait of Messina and the wider gulf of rival ambitions, now march together under one banner. The question before us is no longer whether we can survive, but what we shall become.

The Mezzogiorno is rich in grain, silk, and olive oil. Our ports command the central Mediterranean. Our people carry the blood and traditions of every civilization that has touched these shores. The foundations are laid. Now we must build upon them.

destiny.name: Crown of the South
destiny.text: Like the Hohenstaufen emperors before us, we shall extend our authority northward. Rome, the Eternal City, must acknowledge the power of the southern crown. Seize Rome and build an army worthy of our ambitions.

event.title: The Southern Crown Claims Rome
event.text:
Rome has fallen under our authority. For the first time since Frederick II wore both the imperial and Sicilian crowns, a southern Italian power holds the Eternal City. The Pope may protest, the northern states may tremble, but the message is clear: the Two Sicilies are no mere regional kingdom.

Our soldiers have proven their worth, and our administrators are already extending royal law into the newly acquired territories. The north watches with growing unease.

options.text: Let Rome learn who rules Italy now.

destiny.name: Master of the Peninsula
destiny.text: With Rome secured, the road to central Italy lies open. Florence, jewel of Tuscany, must fall under our dominion. Naples is to be built into a capital fit for the whole peninsula, and the army enlarged to match the great northern powers.

conditions.text: We own Naples and its development is at least 57

event.title: The Iron Crown or the Senate
event.text:
Florence has submitted to the southern crown. The fertile lands of Tuscany, the workshops of the Arno valley, and the banking houses of the Medici's city now serve our kingdom. Central Italy is ours.

But as we push further north, we face a choice. Shall we march with the speed and force that carried the Normans from Hauteville to Palermo, emphasizing military mobility and the feudal levy that is our kingdom's martial backbone? Or shall we follow the Roman model, assimilating conquered peoples, developing their lands, and building a lasting empire through prosperity rather than the sword alone?

options.text: March north under the Iron Crown.

modifiers.name: March of the Iron Crown
modifiers.text: The southern armies march with the speed and determination that once carried Norman knights from Calabria to the gates of Rome. Our levies swell with men eager to serve the crown of Italy.

modifiers.name: Legacy of the Caesars
modifiers.text: Like the Romans who first united Italy, we assimilate conquered peoples into our realm, developing their lands and building prosperity that transcends conquest.

destiny.name: Rex Italiae
destiny.text: The ultimate prize: dominion over all of Italy. Take Milano, the seat of the Iron Crown, and Genoa, the gateway to the western Mediterranean. Only then can the Two Sicilies claim the title of King of Italy.

event.title: Rex Italiae
event.text:
Milano has fallen. Genoa has opened its gates. From the Alps to Sicily, from the Adriatic to the Tyrrhenian, Italy is united under the crown of the Two Sicilies. Not since the days of the Roman Empire has the peninsula known a single master, and we have achieved this from the south, from the very lands that others dismissed as a backward Mezzogiorno.

Frederick II, the Stupor Mundi who amazed the world from his Sicilian court, would recognize what we have built. But how shall we consolidate this vast domain? Through the martial prestige that won it, standing as a great military power that none dare challenge? Or through investment in the land itself, making Italy the most productive and prosperous kingdom in Europe?

options.text: We are the Stupor Mundi reborn.

modifiers.name: Stupor Mundi
modifiers.text: The Amazement of the World (a title once given to Frederick II) now belongs to the kingdom he loved best. Our military prestige commands respect across Europe, though our navy suffers from neglect.

options.text: Let the Mezzogiorno feed all Italy.

modifiers.name: Mezzogiorno Ascendant
modifiers.text: The south rises. Investment in raw materials, infrastructure, and population growth transforms the Mezzogiorno from Italy's poorest region into its most productive.

destiny.name: Mare Nostrum
destiny.text: The Normans of Sicily once ruled from Palermo to Tunis. We shall reclaim that maritime legacy. Seize Tunis and establish silk as a cornerstone of our Mediterranean trade network.

conditions.text: A market the country is in

children.text: Silk is produced in the market
Silk is traded in the market

event.title: The Normans Return to Africa
event.text:
Tunis is ours. Count Roger of Sicily first raided these coasts in the 11th century; now we hold them permanently. The granary of Rome, the gateway to the Saharan trade, and the key to controlling the narrow waist of the Mediterranean, all belong to the Two Sicilies.

Our galleys patrol the waters between Sicily and Ifriqiya. Corsair raids against our coasts will become a memory. And with silk flowing through our markets, the commercial foundations of our maritime empire are firmly established.

options.text: The sea between our shores is ours.

destiny.name: Ionian Trade Routes
destiny.text: Control of Corfu commands the passage between the Adriatic and the wider Mediterranean. With overflowing coffers, our merchants can dominate the Ionian trade routes.

event.title: Dominion over the Ionian Sea
event.text:
With Corfu in our hands, we command the strait that separates the Adriatic from the Ionian Sea. Every ship passing between Venice and the eastern Mediterranean must sail under the watchful eyes of our fortresses. Our merchants are the envy of the south, and our treasury overflows.

Shall we use this position to build naval supremacy, dominating the Adriatic and projecting power across the eastern Mediterranean, even at the cost of neglecting our land forces? Or shall we become the great intermediary, the silk road of the sea, where every trade route converges and every merchant finds profit?

modifiers.name: Adriatic Dominion
modifiers.text: Our warships dominate the Adriatic and Ionian seas. Every merchant vessel sailing these waters does so with our permission, though our commitment to naval power strains our ability to maintain land forces.

options.text: Let commerce flow through our ports.

modifiers.name: Silk Road of the Sea
modifiers.text: Our ports have become the great entrepot of the Mediterranean, where silk, spices, and intelligence flow freely. The wealth brings comfort: perhaps too much comfort.

destiny.name: Emporium of the Mediterranean
destiny.text: From Sardinia to Crete, from Naples to Tunis, our trading houses span the entire Mediterranean. This is the culmination of our maritime destiny: a commercial empire rivaling Venice and Genoa at their height. Messina, the port of the Strait and of the silk fair, is to be its great harbour.

conditions.text: We own Messina and its development is at least 48

event.title: Emporium of the Mediterranean
event.text:
From Sardinia to Crete, from the Strait of Messina to the shores of Ifriqiya, the Two Sicilies have built a commercial empire that spans the entire central and eastern Mediterranean. Our fondaci (the great merchant houses established in every major port) handle a volume of trade that rivals the golden age of Venice.

The question now is whether we press our advantage at sea, building an unchallengeable navy that secures these routes against all rivals, or consolidate our gains through financial institutions and diplomatic networks that make our merchants welcome in every port from Barcelona to Alexandria.

options.text: Our fleet shall rule these waters.

modifiers.name: Sicilian Thalassocracy
modifiers.text: The Two Sicilies have achieved what Venice and Genoa only dreamed of: true maritime supremacy across the central Mediterranean, with the reach to project power to distant shores.

modifiers.name: Emporium Mundi
modifiers.text: The marketplace of the world. Our banking houses offer the best rates, our diplomatic connections open every door, and our careful management of trade keeps inflation firmly in check.

units.name: Norman Cavaliere
units.text: Armored knights in the Norman tradition, these heavy cavalrymen descend from the warriors who conquered southern Italy and Sicily in the 11th century. Their charge remains devastating.

units.name: Tercio Napolitano
units.text: Disciplined infantry of the Neapolitan tercio, combining pikemen and arquebusiers in the formidable Spanish formation that dominated European warfare for over a century.

units.name: Galeazza Reale
units.text: A heavy war galley of the Two Sicilies fleet, larger and more heavily armed than standard Mediterranean galleys, designed to project power across the contested waters of the central Mediterranean.

units.name: Fregata Reale
units.text: A fast sailing frigate of the Bourbon Royal Navy, lighter than a ship of the line but swift enough to patrol the kingdom's extensive coastline and protect its merchant fleet.

units.name: Sanfedisti
units.text: Peasants and charcoal burners of Calabria and the lazzari of Naples, armed with whatever they own and marching under the cross. There are a great many of them and they do not lack fervour. They have never been drilled, and under volley fire it shows.

buildings.name: Torre Costiera
buildings.text: A coastal watchtower in the tradition of the torri costiere that dot the shorelines of Sicily and southern Italy: part of an integrated defense network that uses fire and smoke signals to warn of approaching corsair raids.

buildings.name: Masseria
buildings.text: A fortified agricultural estate of the Mezzogiorno, combining farmland, livestock pens, and defensive walls into a self-sufficient economic unit that has fed the Mediterranean for centuries. The grain fields or the pastures it stands on yield more.

children.text: The location's raw material is Wheat
The location's raw material is Livestock

buildings.name: Reale Seteria
buildings.text: A royal silk manufactory in the tradition of San Leucio, where skilled weavers produce fine silk cloth to rival the best workshops of Lyon and Florence.

buildings.name: Locazione della Dogana
buildings.text: A winter pasture of the Tavoliere, measured out and let by the royal sheep customs to the flock masters of the Abruzzi. The plough is forbidden on it, the flocks pay the crown by the head, and the wool is sold at the fair of Foggia.

where.text: Wool is produced in the location's market

buildings.name: Reggia Reale
buildings.text: A magnificent royal palace in the tradition of the Reggia di Caserta, a seat of centralized power from which the king administers his vast Italian domains, rivaling Versailles in grandeur and ambition.

buildings.name: Fondaco dei Mercanti
buildings.text: A grand merchant trading house in the tradition of the Venetian fondaci, a fortified warehouse, exchange, and customs house combined, serving as the hub of Mediterranean commerce in our ports.

list.name: Constitutions of Melfi
list.text: Promulgated by Frederick II at Melfi on 1 September 1231, the Liber Augustalis was a comprehensive Roman-law codification of the Regno's administration, a reform of Roger II's Assizes of Ariano (1140) and Frederick's own Assizes of Capua (1220), drafted with Petrus de Vinea and the Bolognese masters. Through its 219 constitutions Frederick bound the great feudatories to royal courts, regulated coinage and commerce, and asserted the imperator-rex above all other authorities. Ernst Kantorowicz called it 'the birth certificate of the modern administrative state'; it remained the foundation of Sicilian law until the Napoleonic codes.

list.name: Camera della Sommaria
list.text: Established by Alfonso V of Aragon at Naples in 1444 from the older curia magistrorum rationalium, the Regia Camera della Sommaria was the supreme financial court of the Kingdom of Naples. Presided over by a luogotenente and staffed by the razionali (jurists and accountants drawn largely from the urban legal bourgeoisie), it audited royal and municipal accounts, prosecuted fiscal malfeasance, and adjudicated baronial relevi (succession dues). From 1596 it was divided into two rotae handling civil and criminal fiscal litigation, and remained the realm's principal instrument of fiscal discipline until its replacement by the Corte dei Conti in 1807.

list.name: Regia Dogana delle Pecore
list.text: Established at Lucera in 1447 by Alfonso V and transferred to Foggia by 1468, the Royal Customs of the Sheep Drove regulated the great seasonal transhumance between the Abruzzese highlands and the winter pastures of the Tavoliere delle Puglie. Modelled on the Castilian Mesta, it charged eight ducats fida per hundred sheep in exchange for assigned pasture, policed the tratturi against intrusive cultivation, and produced one of the two principal revenue streams of the Kingdom of Naples. Its monopoly on the Tavoliere froze vast tracts as winter pasture for centuries; Joseph Bonaparte abolished it on 21 May 1806.

list.name: Caricatori del Regno
list.text: The royal grain-loading ports of Sicily (principally Sciacca, Girgenti, Licata, and Termini Imerese) where wheat from the latifondi was warehoused under royal seal and shipped only to merchants holding tratte, the export licences sold by the crown. The maestri portulani inspected every load, and Genoese factors competed in the licence market for the right to ship the surplus to Genoa, Naples, Rome, and the Levant. The system underwrote Sicily's sixteenth-century golden age as the granary of the Mediterranean and gave the crown a fiscal lever that depended upon, but also constrained, the baronial estates that produced the grain.

list.name: Parlamento di Sicilia
list.text: First convened at Mazara by Roger I in 1097 and meeting at Palermo from 1130 in the Palazzo dei Normanni, the Parlamento di Sicilia is among the oldest legislatures in Europe. It assembled in three bracci: the feudal arm of counts and barons, the ecclesiastical arm of archbishops, abbots, and archimandrites, and the demaniale arm of representatives from the 42 royal towns. Its principal function was to vote the donativo to the king in exchange for confirmation of privileges, and across seven centuries it constrained royal taxation through habits of consultation that survived even Spanish absolutism. Abolished in 1812 with the British-inspired Sicilian Constitution and finally extinguished with Sicilian autonomy in 1816.

list.name: Consiglio Collaterale
list.text: Created under the Spanish viceroys at Naples to flank (collateral to) the viceroy in matters of government, justice, and finance, the Consiglio Collaterale comprised five regents (typically Spanish and Neapolitan jurists) who processed decrees and oversaw the great courts of the realm. Its judicial section, the Cancelleria, was deliberately strengthened by the viceroys to compress the older Sacro Regio Consiglio (the supreme court of Aragonese Naples), shifting authority from the autonomous magistracy toward a council whose members served at Madrid's pleasure. It became the principal instrument by which the Habsburgs and later the Bourbons drew the togati (the urban legal bourgeoisie) into central administration at the expense of the great feudal houses.
